title: My Father! Cheering Name
description: My Father! Cheering Name in Tonic Solfa to FRANCONIA, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Anne Steele wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 102 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “God our Father”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to FRANCONIA; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: My Fa-ther! cheer-ing name! O, may I call thee mine? Give me the hum-ble hope to claim A por-tion so di-vine.

lines: O, may I call thee mine?
Give me the humble hope to claim
For thou art just, and good, and wise:
O, bend my will to thine!
O give me strength to bear
Still let me know a father reigns,
Yet shall my soul, believing, own
That all thy ways are right.
If thou accept my humble claim,

licence: Public domain: Anne Steele died in 1778.
credits: Words by Anne Steele (1717–1778), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to FRANCONIA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
